session_instructions: User (2026-10-20): do not stop to ask questions; block issues needing user input in jit and record the question in the issue and handoff; send project-level escalations to steward session just-in-time-24 (milestone 9db27a3a); write handoff and tell the steward when nothing more can proceed; check workers every 30 min.
traps: Do not merge into main while a cargo-ci gate run is in progress on main; the run's verdict then mixes trees.
cargo-ci's budget step (30 s suite clock) and 20 s nextest timeouts fail under host load from parallel workers or other sessions; evaluate gates only when load average is low.

reclaim-worker-worktree.sh harvests every worktree target (17-23 GB each) into the cache pool with rsync; for a 9-worktree wave it filled the disk to 100%. Remove merged worktrees' target dirs directly instead.
Worker worktrees grow to ~17-23 GB each after a full cargo-ci; cap parallel workers by free disk.
Main checkout is shared with other sessions: commit only this epic's paths (git add --pathspec-from-file), never git add .jit wholesale.
Redirect messages to a running worker can be missed: w-d7d0d0db implemented d92f54aa's superseded scope despite a redirect; verify commit scope on return.

cargo-ci declares inputs, so jit gate evaluate reuses any prior run (even another lead's load-failed run) at the same input digest; rerun a budget/timeout-only failure with --force under the turnstile.
Ask the steward before adding any issue to this epic, even a leaf bug (steward rule after b5faef84).
After sending a worker a mid-task constraint, wait for its post-constraint report before merging; b5faef84 was merged on a pre-constraint report and needed a follow-up worktree.
resource_policy: Steward (binding, revised 2026-10-21): dispatch a new worker worktree only when df shows >=60 GB free; at most 2 live worker worktrees for this lead; remove each worktree as soon as its work merges; every full cargo-ci gate runs under `flock /tmp/jit-full-ci.lock`; budget-only failures under load are rerun under the lock. Never touch the July/August worktrees (agent-123efe74, 1fc8fec3, a122b9b3, bfd215fa, deb33646, efaec52f, steward-v1-readiness). Build turnstile (binding): FULL gates run as `flock /tmp/jit-ci-turnstile.lock flock -x /tmp/jit-full-ci.lock <cmd>`; every other cargo build/test runs as `flock /tmp/jit-ci-turnstile.lock true && flock -s /tmp/jit-full-ci.lock <cmd>`; always CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0. If the budget still fails in a quiet window, record it; the steward holds a user item on budget-under-load. Budget ruling (steward, pending user decision): a budget failure on a quiet host (load < ~4, lock uncontended) is a real finding against the change that crossed 30 s; fix within the change (drop duplicate-property tests, move subprocess tests to harness, speed fixtures), never --force it; only load failures get --force; if a change cannot get under 30 s without losing coverage, block the issue with timings and continue. Merge rule (binding): every git merge into main or other source edit on main runs as `flock /tmp/jit-ci-turnstile.lock flock -x /tmp/jit-full-ci.lock git merge ...`; tracker-only .jit writes are exempt. Conflict rule (binding): never resolve merge conflicts in main's checkout; merge main into the task branch in its worktree, resolve and test there, then clean-merge into main under the lock.
